key_insight: Weld quality in FFF-printed thermoplastics depends on coupled processing and structural factors, so increasing welding energy does not necessarily improve joint strength.
engineering_relevance: Reliable welding could enable thermoplastic assemblies larger than printer build volumes while preserving joint integrity.
method: Critically reviews friction stir, friction stir spot, rotary friction, ultrasonic, laser, and microwave-assisted welding.
Examines joining mechanisms, process parameters, printed structures, mechanical performance, and failure.
Maps relationships among welding conditions, polymer type, infill, interface design, and joint configuration.
evidence_signal: The reviewed evidence links joint performance to heating and consolidation, but differences in materials, geometries, joint configurations, and tests limit direct comparisons.
watch_item: Evidence for microwave-assisted welding of separately printed components remains limited.
paper_title: Welding of thermoplastics printed by fused filament fabrication: A critical review of joining mechanisms and relationships between processing, structure, and properties
